item.title: Federal government shrinks New York's Essential Plan, preserving coverage for 1.3 million while axing 470,000
item.description: The federal government approved New York's request to scale back its Essential Plan health insurance program, protecting coverage for 1.3 million low-income New Yorkers while leaving 470,000 others searching for new policies.

item.title: SCOTUS declines to hear challenge to New York's Even-Year Election Law
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court declined to hear a challenge to New York's Even Year Election Law, which moves local elections to even-numbered years to encourage higher voter turnout and save the state money, despite arguments that it unfairly treats local governments and could lead to voter fatigue.

item.title: Governor Hochul discussed proposed climate act change
item.description: New York's landmark 2019 Climate Act was under review according to Governor Kathy Hochul. After a government memo was released earlier this year, New Yorkers learned they could face utility bill increases of over $4,000. On Monday, Governor Hochul spoke to the media for the first time since she called for changes to the state's major climate act to prevent rising utility costs. It required 40% emissions reductions by 2030 and 85% reduction by 2050.
